title: Invisible Character Finder
description: Detect hidden zero-width and control characters in text — see exactly where they hide, reveal them, or strip them out.
howto: Paste text that may contain hidden characters (copied from the web, PDFs or chats).
Every invisible character is listed with its name, code point and position.
Use "Reveal" to see markers in place, or "Strip & copy" to get clean text.

faqs.a: Unicode characters with no visible glyph: zero-width space (U+200B), zero-width joiner (U+200D), byte-order mark (U+FEFF), soft hyphen (U+00AD) and others. They sneak in via copy-paste.
They can break code, confuse plagiarism checks, alter word counts, hide text in social bios, or smuggle tracking into copied content.
For prose, yes. Note: zero-width joiners (U+200D) are meaningful inside some emoji sequences — stripping splits those emoji into parts.
